breakouts.h: Breakout watch: 12 players ready to make the leap
breakouts.d: Rating jumps from offseason training, new starting jobs, scheme fits and what they did with limited snaps last year. These are the names to know before kickoff.

list.name: M.Goodman
list.d: [[p:557715432|M.Goodman]] is penciled in as a starter for the first time. On top of that, he saw his pass blocking (84 to 88) and power pass protection (88 to 92) take a big step in training. And he brings a agile skill set to a scheme that ranks 15th in total offensive yards per game. By October, everyone will know it.

list.name: B.Jackson
list.d: [[p:557716657|B.Jackson]] ran for 6.6 yards a carry as a backup. On top of that, Ohio State leans on the run game (6th in rushing yards per game last year). And he brings a east/west playmaker skill set to a scheme that ranks 9th in rushing yards per game. By October, everyone will know it.

list.name: S.Eddy
list.d: [[p:557711984|S.Eddy]] is penciled in as a starter for the first time. Add this: he came out of the offseason at 76 overall, up from 72. He saw his play recognition (74 to 84) take a big step in training. This is the year.

list.name: N.Dean
list.d: [[p:557714135|N.Dean]] is penciled in as a starter for the first time. Better yet, he saw his hands (83 to 88) and catching in traffic (77 to 82) take a big step in training. And he averaged 21.8 yards a catch in a limited role. Kennesaw State fans are about to get a new favorite player.

list.name: D.Wilson
list.d: [[p:557723180|D.Wilson]] averaged 17.0 yards a catch in a limited role. Also: Florida threw it more than almost anyone last year (5th in passing yards per game). He brings a contested specialist skill set to a scheme that ranks 20th in receptions. Circle his name now.

list.name: M.Lightfoot
list.d: [[p:557717747|M.Lightfoot]] is penciled in as a starter for the first time. Better yet, he saw his block shedding (73 to 77) and pursuit (89 to 93) take a big step in training. And he brings a speed rusher skill set to a scheme that ranks 16th in sacks. This is the year.

list.name: L.Thornton Jr.
list.d: [[p:557722082|L.Thornton Jr.]] jumped from 91 to 94 overall this offseason. Also: he saw his man coverage (91 to 95) and press coverage (90 to 94) take a big step in training. Plus, he picked off 4 passes in part-time work. By October, everyone will know it.

list.name: A.Henderson
list.d: [[p:557727642|A.Henderson]] is penciled in as a starter for the first time. Add this: Auburn leans on the run game (22nd in rushing yards per game last year). He ran for 10.4 yards a carry as a backup. By October, everyone will know it.

list.name: N.Pullard
list.d: [[p:557719002|N.Pullard]] jumped from 75 to 79 overall this offseason. Better yet, he saw his man coverage (83 to 87) and press coverage (71 to 75) take a big step in training. And he carries a Elite development trait. By October, everyone will know it.

list.d: [[p:557726587|A.Noriega]] brings a dual threat skill set to a scheme that ranks 13th in offensive pass yards per game. Also: Penn State threw it more than almost anyone last year (11th in passing yards per game). He carries a Star development trait. By October, everyone will know it.
